question: Identity & roles: Does it clearly name the controller (and key roles like DPO/contact) and how to reach them?
Lawfulness hook: Does it state why processing is lawful (e.g., consent/contract/legal obligation/legitimate interest), at least at a high level?
Clear purposes: Does it explain what data is used for in clear, plain terms (not just generic “improve services”)?
Transparency quality: Is the information easy to find and easy to understand (clear language, structured sections, no hidden key points)?
Fairness expectations: Does it avoid “surprise” processing (or clearly warns about unusual processing) so users can reasonably expect what happens to their data?
Specified & explicit purposes: Are purposes listed in a specific way (separate purposes, not one vague bucket)?
Purpose at collection: Does it indicate purposes are determined at the time of collection (or at least before use)?
No “unlimited purpose” language: Does it avoid wording that allows use for undefined/unlimited future purposes?
Further processing rules: If it mentions re-use (analytics, research, marketing, “improvement”), does it explain conditions/limits (e.g., consent, legal basis, compatibility, safeguards)?
Compatibility logic: Does it explain how new purposes are linked to the original ones (instead of “we may use your data for other purposes”)?
Data categories listed: Does it say what categories of personal data it collects/uses (not just “information you provide”)?
Link data → purpose: Does it connect data categories to purposes (so readers see why each type is needed)?
“Only necessary” commitment: Does it state it collects/uses only what is necessary (not excessive) for those purposes?
Avoids disproportionate data: Does it avoid asking for overly sensitive/excessive data unless clearly justified?
Alternative/optional data: Does it distinguish required vs optional data (and explain “if you don’t provide X, service Y won’t work”)?
Right to rectification: Does it clearly tell users they can correct/update inaccurate data (and how)?
Update mechanism: Does it describe a practical way to keep data up to date (account settings, contact form, etc.)?
Correction without delay (commitment): Does it commit to fixing/deleting inaccurate data within a reasonable timeframe (or “without undue delay” wording)?
Source clarity: If data comes from third parties, does it explain that and how accuracy is handled?

Retention periods: Does it give specific retention times or clear criteria per data type/purpose (not just “as long as necessary”)?
Deletion/review process: Does it mention time limits for deletion or periodic review of whether storage is still needed?
Identifiers minimized over time: Does it mention deletion, anonymization, or aggregation when identification is no longer needed?
Exceptions explained: If it keeps data longer (e.g., legal claims, archiving/research/statistics), does it explain the reason and safeguards?
User-facing clarity: Is retention info easy to find and understandable (not buried in legal language)?
Security measures described: Does it describe security at least at a high level (technical/organizational measures), not just “we take security seriously”?
Threat coverage: Does it mention protection against unauthorized access/unlawful processing and accidental loss/destruction/damage?
Access controls & governance: Does it mention access limitation (who can access data, least privilege, training/policies) even briefly?
Breach handling: Does it mention breach response/notification in any form (even if not detailed)?
Third parties/processors: If it uses vendors, does it say they must apply appropriate security measures too?
Responsibility stated: Does the policy implicitly/explicitly indicate the controller is responsible for GDPR compliance and user rights handling?
Demonstration tools (signals): Does it mention any accountability mechanisms (records, policies, audits, DPIA, privacy-by-design, governance) at least as commitments?
Roles & contacts: Is there a clear contact/DPO channel for privacy questions/complaints?
User rights process: Does it clearly explain how to exercise rights + expected response steps/timeframes?
Oversight & redress: Does it mention the supervisory authority/right to lodge a complaint (or equivalent redress path)?
